sections.overview: Trogonoptera brookiana is a large birdwing butterfly native to parts of Southeast Asia.
sections.identification: Its dark wings have striking metallic-green markings.
sections.habitat: It is associated mainly with primary forest across the Malay Peninsula, Borneo and Sumatra.
sections.diet: In Peninsular Malaysia, Aristolochia foveolata is reported as a host plant for the subspecies albescens.
sections.behavior: Males of the subspecies albescens gather at riverbanks and mineral-rich puddles; this behavior is not described for every population.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted focus on host plants and male behavior and give few species-specific details on egg laying.
sections.ecology: MyBIS lists Troides brookiana as a synonym; the inventory name Trogonoptera brookiana is retained here.
sections.conservation: The 2018 IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern, while noting habitat loss and collection as pressures.
